claims.text: The initial AlCoCrFeNi eutectic alloy has a continuous dual-phase lamellar microstructure that exhibits catastrophic interfacial cracking and low ductility during room-temperature tension.
Cold rolling by more than 80% thickness reduction will introduce a high dislocation density and strain gradients.
Annealing at 900–1100 °C for 1–20 minutes after severe rolling will partially recrystallize the softer phase while retaining deformation in the harder phase.
The rolling and phase-selective annealing treatment will convert continuous lamellae into a patterned heterogeneous grain structure.
The resulting heterogeneous grain structure will contain coarse grains adjacent to ultrafine grains.
Coherent nanotwins or low-misfit interfaces will stabilize the patterned heterogeneous structure.

A suitable annealing window exists in which the FCC phase has a stacking-fault energy conducive to deformation twinning and partial recrystallization while the B2 phase remains stable or recrystallizes at a different rate.
Interfaces between coarse and fine regions will accumulate geometrically necessary dislocations.
The heterogeneous structure will produce high back-stress hardening.
Back-stress hardening will delay necking and promote more uniform plastic deformation.
Back stress will redistribute stress away from brittle phase interfaces and thereby prevent catastrophic interfacial cracking.
A dislocation approaching a coherent twin boundary can dissociate, with one partial crossing the boundary and another moving along it.
Coherent internal boundaries will promote strain hardening without premature failure.
The treated AlCoCrFeNi alloy will achieve uniform elongation above 20% and ultimate tensile strength above 1.5 GPa.
The treatment will markedly reduce microcrack density at phase interfaces relative to the as-cast state.
The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi baseline has less than 10% ductility and fails catastrophically because of stress concentration at continuous phase boundaries.

Annealing below the treatment window leaves the brittle continuous lamellae intact, whereas excessive temperature or duration causes full recrystallization and homogenization that remove heterogeneous-structure benefits.
HIP at 1100 °C and 100 MPa for 2 hours will produce full recrystallization and homogenization without the phase-selective mechanism.
The hypothesis is falsified if the HIP-treated sample is statistically indistinguishable in strength and ductility from the as-cast sample.
Failure of a non-patterned HIP sample to exceed 20% elongation supports the patterned-structure mechanism, whereas superior HIP performance relative to a patterned sample falsifies it.

contradictions.description: The rule says HIP performance statistically indistinguishable from the low-ductility as-cast baseline falsifies the hypothesis, but it also says that a non-patterned HIP sample failing to reach the predicted elongation supports the patterned-structure mechanism. Given the stated baseline of less than 10% ductility, the same HIP result could therefore both falsify and support the hypothesis.

The three specified experimental groups do not include the phase-selectively annealed treatment, yet the falsification rule requires direct comparison of the HIP sample with a phase-selectively annealed or patterned sample.
